or if some choice of twin pairs leaves a component with four or
five neighbors. The recorded witnesses use degree-three vertices
outside $\{a,b,c,d,e\}$, so their neighborhoods do not change
when further vertices with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$ or $\{a,d,e\}$ are added.
Thus a forbidden adjacency remains. For the second exclusion,
the chosen $\Psi_3$ remains unchanged, and the old component lies
in a component still meeting at least four of its attachments.
Both exclusions therefore remain valid for all five choices
of $(n_c,n_e)$.

These exclusions leave $193$ graphs, giving $965$ graphs after
the five choices of $(n_c,n_e)$ are made.
Of these, $172$ are toroidal, $782$ have a proper nontoroidal
minor, and the remaining $11$ are copies of the five graphs
in the statement~\supp{E34}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... Vertices of the forms are B<k>_<x>; added single vertices are v_<neighbourhood>.
